findings.claim: Depolarizing p<=1/5. Conventions checked: exact match.
findings.quote: The channel applies each nonidentity Pauli error with probability p/3
findings.effect: Same convention as the run's N_p (depolarizing-parent-verdict.md:5), so the comparison below is like-for-like.

findings.quote: In particular, R = 0 for 1/4 ≤ p ≤ 3/4, and no positive-rate stabilizer family has a depolarizing threshold at or above p = 1/4.
findings.effect: NOT APPLICABLE. The result is a converse (an upper bound on rate) for stabilizer-code families under optimal syndrome decoding. It is zero only at p>=1/4, the known antidegradable point, so it does not touch the run's coherent-information lower bound at 1/5 or Ahmed's claimed 0.2029161. It is neither a precedent nor a contradiction.

findings.quote: The bound in Theorem 23 is not intended to compete with the best known upper bounds on the quantum capacity of the depolarizing channel for 0 < p < 1/4
findings.read_scope: Remark 24 (it also notes that degenerate codes can exceed the hashing rate)
findings.effect: Confirms the converse is not offered as a new capacity limit below 1/4. No effect.

findings.claim: Depolarizing p<=1/5 (incidental numbers in the same paper)
findings.quote: The maximum of g_Q occurs at a depolarizing probability between 0.1955 and 0.2100 for every code.
findings.effect: This is where the GEXIT curve of small codes peaks. It is not a threshold or capacity statement, and should not be cited as one.

findings.claim: Depolarizing p<=1/5 (unrelated use of the same channel)
findings.quote: For the six-state protocol with equal three-basis error rate p∈[p*,1/2], where p*=(5−√5)/10≃27.64%, we construct a single compatible collective attack that defeats a broad class of linear postprocessing.
findings.read_scope: listing abstract and comments ('v2: ... no changes to the technical content')
findings.effect: Different task: two-way secret-key agreement, with p measured as per-basis QBER. Converting under the run's convention gives total error ≈0.4146 > 1/4 [INFERENCE]. No effect.

findings.claim: Depolarizing p<=1/5 (newest abstract-search hits, outside the mailing)
findings.quote: it approaches the quantum capacity of the erasure channel and the hashing bound for memoryless Pauli channels, including the depolarizing channel.
findings.effect: Achieves the hashing bound only, which is below 1/5. No effect. The ID does not appear in the old review/*.md notes. 2606.10744 (superposition-of-channels superactivation, NMR experiment) uses a different resource setting; no effect.

findings.quote: propose several new constructions based on incomplete orthogonal Latin squares, incomplete transversal designs, and $\Sigma$-resolvable transversal designs
findings.effect: Classical mixed orthogonal arrays; only the terminology overlaps. This is the only 'Latin' hit in either listing (quant-ph has none).
